experiment: H_PI_1: PyG 1.6.0 vs PyG 2.5.3 BETA-reimpl FTA reproducibility
test_protocol: single seed 50 epochs, B=5 PGD attack on argmax target sensor, V_bar prune via eigenvector centrality
key_finding_pyg16_needs_same_patches: PyG 1.6.0 has the same scatter/segment_csr API as 2.5.3 — these patches are NOT modernization-specific; they target a pre-2.x architectural quirk that GDN's GraphLayer's 3D message tensors expose.
diagnostic_verdict: Modernization DOES affect K-aggregation FTA behavior. Under PyG 2.5.3, perturbing 5 influencer sensors causes a 'compensation effect' where other sensors' standardized scores inflate ~14× (51 → 750), keeping top-K sums above threshold. Under PyG 1.6.0, this compensation is absent — perturbations propagate differently through the GAT attention, and the attack drives all sensors uniformly. Neither version produces BETA's reported 26.3% delta_FTA.
implication_for_paper: We cannot attribute our reproduction failure solely to either modernization OR data; both contribute. PyG 2.5 K-aggregation methodology saturates at 0% (over-defended by compensation); PyG 1.6 saturates at 100% (under-defended). BETA's 26.3% sits between these, suggesting their actual evaluation uses a methodology axis we haven't identified (likely related to attack target selection or threshold convention rather than aggregation K).
next_steps_for_pi: H_PI_3: drop FTA from head-to-head head-to-head; use multi-metric (raw F1, PA-F1@K=10, AUC-PR) instead
